feature.title: Provider keys live in parley-api, not the app
feature.problem: The Groq, Deepgram and MiniMax keys are pasted into the desktop app and stored there, one copy per device, even though parley-api now runs on this Mac and already holds the MiniMax and Exa keys for Explain. This feature moves every provider key to parley-api's .env. Dictation, voice edit and the Act agent call the providers through parley-api, which adds the key; the app stores none. The app keeps its request code: parley-api is a narrow pass-through for the exact provider calls the app already makes, bound to 127.0.0.1 so nothing off this Mac can spend the keys. Settings stops asking for keys and instead shows whether the Parley server is reachable and which keys it has. When the server is down, the pill says so, as Explain already does. Frame note: the settings window is not PageShell, so the archetypes below are illustrative and not probe-enforced, as in parley-007 to parley-016.
nonGoals: Parley starting parley-api by itself: you run it (make api / npm --prefix parley-api start) as today. Auto-start, like the Act agent's supervisor, is a follow-up.
Android: it keeps its own keys and native transcriber; it cannot reach this Mac's localhost.
Queueing audio while the server is down: the take fails with a clear error.
Copying the keys the app stores today into .env automatically: they are encrypted with this app's keychain entry; you add them to parley-api/.env once, and the app then deletes its copies.

surfaces.name: Overview tab · Parley server
surfaces.purpose: Show whether dictation, voice edit and Act can run: is the Parley server up, and does it have the key each one needs.

panels.title: Overview
panels.subtitle: Keys live in parley-api on this Mac.
rows: Missing a key? Add it to parley-api/.env and restart the server.

states.loading: Checking: the Server row shows a small Loader in place of the badge; the key rows keep their last answer.
states.empty: Server up but a key missing: that row shows a 'Not set' badge and the line 'Add GROQ_API_KEY to parley-api/.env and restart the server.' Dictation with that provider fails on the pill with the same sentence.
states.error: Server unreachable: the Server row shows a red 'Not running' badge and an Alert: 'Start it with make api in the parley folder. Dictation, voice edit and Explain need it.' Key rows show 'Unknown'.
states.success: Running: a green badge on Server, a check on each key the server has, and the provider SegmentedControl still switches Groq and Deepgram.

surfaces.name: Setup wizard · Transcription step
surfaces.purpose: Replace 'paste your Groq key' with 'make sure the Parley server is running', so first-run setup no longer asks for a key.

panels.title: Transcription runs on your Parley server
panels.subtitle: Parley sends your speech to parley-api on this Mac, which holds the Groq key.

states.loading: The status rows show a Loader while the first check runs.
states.empty: Server up, no Groq key: 'Add GROQ_API_KEY to parley-api/.env and restart the server', Continue still enabled (setup can finish; dictation will say what is missing).
states.error: Server not running: the start command in a Code block and Check again; Continue still enabled.
states.success: Both checks green, Continue is the primary button.

components.control: SettingRow + Badge for server and key status, Button 'Check again'
components.why: Read-only status in the same label-left, state-right rows the Overview and Agent tabs already use; one action re-runs the check.
components.rejected: Keeping PasswordInputs that write to the server (the server's .env is the single place keys live; a write path would need auth for no gain on one Mac), a Card per provider (heavier than the rest of the tab)

components.control: Alert (red) when the server is unreachable, plain dimmed Text for a missing key
components.why: Unreachable blocks everything, so it earns the one banner; a missing key blocks one mode, so a line under its row is enough.
components.rejected: A toast (it would vanish while the problem stays), a Modal like MiniMaxOffer (that modal is removed: there is no key to collect)

components.control: The wizard's existing step Card with status rows and a Code block for the start command
components.why: Same frame as the other steps; the step now verifies instead of collecting.
components.rejected: Dropping the step (first run would never learn the server must be running), blocking Continue on a red check (setup should finish; the pill explains later)
